title: Lists and ScrollViews
description: Understand how to display scrollable lists and manage large data sets efficiently using ScrollView and FlatList components in React Native.

lessons.title: What is ScrollView?
lessons.content: ScrollView is a React Native component that provides a scrolling container for views and components. It renders all its children at once, which is suitable for smaller lists or static content.

lessons.title: Basic Usage of ScrollView
Limitations of ScrollView
lessons.content: ScrollView renders all child components immediately, which can cause performance issues with large lists due to high memory usage and slow rendering.

lessons.title: Introduction to FlatList
lessons.content: FlatList is designed for rendering large lists efficiently by rendering only visible items and recycling views as the user scrolls, improving performance.

lessons.title: Basic FlatList Usage
Important FlatList Props Explained
lessons.content:
Key FlatList props:
- `data`: The array of items to render.
- `renderItem`: Function to render each item.
- `keyExtractor`: Unique key for each item.
- `horizontal`: Makes list horizontal.
- `ListHeaderComponent` and `ListFooterComponent`: Add header/footer.
- `onEndReached`: Callback when the end is reached (for infinite scrolling).

lessons.title: Adding Pull-to-Refresh in FlatList
Handling Empty Lists
Optimizing Performance with getItemLayout
lessons.content: Using `getItemLayout` prop improves scroll performance by providing the height of each item, so the list can calculate scroll positions without rendering all items.

lessons.title: Summary and Best Practices
lessons.content:
- Use ScrollView for small static content
- Use FlatList for large or dynamic lists
- Always provide `keyExtractor` for list items
- Use pull-to-refresh for better UX
- Optimize performance with `getItemLayout` and pagination
